cohort: The study included 90 neonates with respiratory distress requiring CPAP therapy, comprising 53.3% preterm, 44.4% term, and the rest postterm babies.
finding: The study found significant improvement in Silverman and Downe's scores after 6 and 12 hours of CPAP, with a CPAP success rate of 68.9% and a mortality rate of 25.6% among the enrolled neonates.
mod_finding: No significant association of CPAP failure was seen when compared to mode of delivery.
gest_age: 53.3% preterm, 44.4% term, and the rest postterm
